title: Structure of an HTML document and metadata

videos.script: Open any page on the web and ask the browser to show you its source. {{source}} What you get is text. Words, and between them, words in angle brackets. That text is HTML, and this lesson is about reading it. {{tags}} The angle brackets are not decoration. Each pair names what the words between them are. This is a heading. This is a paragraph. This is a link to another page. {{tree}} The browser reads the text from top to bottom and builds a tree out of it. Every heading, every paragraph, every link becomes a node, and each node has exactly one parent. {{repair}} Here is the part that surprises people. The browser almost never refuses a page. Leave out a closing tag, and it closes one for you. Put things in the wrong order, and it rearranges them. Most of the time you never find out. {{blank}} Sometimes the repair is a disaster. One missing closing tag in this lesson turns a whole page into its own title, and the window stays blank. {{head}} So the lesson goes through a document from its first line to its last. The doctype, and what happens without it. The head, which the reader never sees and every browser reads. The body, which is the page. {{validate}} And it ends with a program that reads your HTML the way the browser does, and tells you where it had to guess. {{end}}
